releaseNotes: Search: a clear button removes the text without leaving the field.
Merging dives adjusts later dive numbers even when some dives are unnumbered.
Logbook: renumber a dive and all later dives starting with the number you choose.
Desktop: the logbook selector shows the logbook name without a redundant label.
Shared map: panning and scrolling are smoother when many sites are displayed.
Shared map: the list follows the visible area, including sites grouped on the map.
Shared map: a message explains when sites are unavailable offline.
Shared map: added sites from OpenDiving Commons.
Sites: changes received by sync appear without reopening the app.
Desktop: the shared map loads when the world view crosses the date line.
Sites: coordinates with degree symbols are recognised and displayed according to your settings.
Sites: names appear when zooming in on either map; on tablets, the embedded map can be panned and zoomed and clears the system navigation area.
Shared map: the mode buttons are easier to tap.
Sites: nearby sites are grouped on phones and tablets; the shared map is available on desktop.
Diver profile: the email address replaces the server's technical identifier when no name is set.
Account on phones, tablets and desktop: the email address replaces the server's technical identifier.
Desktop: the account menu no longer shows a plus sign on the initial.
Android tablets: the Account icon in the navigation rail is larger.
Desktop logbook: rename the displayed logbook from the Logbook menu without changing its file.
Tablet logbook: the dive list is slightly wider in landscape.
Equipment: an annual service reminder, including valve service, is suggested for drysuits.
Equipment: the suggested regulator service interval is now one year or 100 dives.
Logbook: a dive's site and other edited details now appear in the list after saving.
Desktop dive details: the editing hint no longer appears under buddies and guides.
Desktop dive details: the water type menu opens with one click.
Deleting dives automatically shifts the numbers of later dives.
Fixed a dive detail error at startup when a cloud logbook is open.
Logbook on tablets: when dives are checked, detail actions move to the top ⋮ menu, which can delete the selection.
Restore: a dive takes the missing number at its position; if none is available, later dives are shifted.
Information: the date of birth, relationship, phone and blood group fields are narrower.
Profile: the back arrow no longer appears on tablets and desktop.
Information: a back arrow closes editing without saving.
Profile and equipment: the Maintenance entry appears when an active piece has a maintenance reminder.
Equipment: a piece's menu offers permanent deletion after confirmation.
Equipment: the type of piece field no longer appears when creating an Other piece.
Dive profile: selected curves stay visible during the session.
Dives: “Get it signed” replaces “Get it validated”.
Equipment: the scooter icon has been redesigned.
Equipment: choose the piece type before filling in its form.
Equipment: line cutters and knives are separate types.
Equipment: a compass can be added as a piece.
Settings on tablets and desktop: the logbook computers list opens correctly.
Certifications: the number is optional and the instructor’s number can be added.
Profile on a landscape tablet: the My diver profile column is a little wider.
Profile on tablets and desktop: the Add equipment button fits its content and is aligned to the right.
Profile on tablets: controls stay clear of the system bars.
Certificates and documents: Add is pale blue and floats at the bottom right on tablets and desktop; the card reproduction note has been removed.
Certificates and documents: the empty state is centred in the panel.
Certificates: the agency menu includes more diving organizations and is sorted alphabetically.
Certificates: level suggestions now cover more agencies, with free entry for other qualifications.
Certificates: type an agency or level directly without choosing Other.
Logbook: the menu can export the whole logbook in the chosen format.
Dive detail on desktop: Equipment shows each dive computer’s photo when available.
Settings: closing choice menus no longer causes an error.

Account (free version): the Account button stays, with a silhouette. Its sheet shows the logbook on this device, “Subscribe”, “Already subscribed? Sign in” and the Benthic+ rows that open the offer. With an Benthic+ account, “My diver profile” carries the Benthic+ chip and, when a piece is overdue for maintenance, a red badge and the line “Maintenance: 1 piece overdue”; the sheet’s cross is on the right. “Manage the account” opens a screen (a two-column dialog on a tablet and on the desktop): e-mail and sign-in method, subscription with “Manage in Google Play” (or the App Store), a 10 GB photo and video space, “Download my data”, “Sign out” and “Delete the account” after a confirmation. On Android, Back closes the account sheet. The Benthic+ offer has “Already subscribed? Sign in” (except right after signing in), and “Continue without an account” is centred under the three buttons on a tablet and on the desktop. The “Benthic” name on an Benthic+ account’s sheet is followed by a small round “+” chip. On a tablet, “Subscribe” and the two rows with the chip open the Benthic+ offer in two panes: the blue panel on the left, the five tiles, the price and “Subscribe” on the right.
Logbook: the search box moves up a little, further from the header wave.

Start: the launch screen now stays until the first real screen is drawn (the first launch on a first start, the logbook otherwise), with a short fade, and the first launch no longer appears after an empty logbook. The first screen is laid out once, with the real height of the status bar, so nothing jumps.
« Sign in or create an account »: a little more space between the buttons, and « Continue without an account » in blue, centred.

First screens: a page opened for the first time now waits for its styles before it is shown, and the drawings of the blue bands have a fixed size, so nothing flashes at a large size while the first launch screen opens.

Desktop logbook: the table is lighter. Default columns: number in bold, date with the day of the week and the time in small grey, site (or "Site not set" in grey italics with a crossed-out pin), deepest depth in bold, duration, buddies. The "Profile" column (small dive graphs) is hidden by default and added with the columns button; the columns and widths you chose are kept. A line under the headers gives the year and dive count of the first visible dive and stays at the top while scrolling. A trip is a white card that folds. The selected dive is pale blue, with its number and site in blue.

First launch (public edition): if you come from the alpha, “Import a logbook” offers “Previous version’s logbook”, with its number of dives. It copies that logbook, read from the alpha’s copy on the phone without the network and without the alpha’s account (even if the alpha’s sign-in is gone), into a new logbook; with several copies, one row per copy shows its number of dives and its date. The alpha’s files are not touched and the row disappears after the copy.

Public edition: no choice is left to open a logbook in OneDrive, Google Drive or a personal git repository. “Open my logbook” offers the Benthic server, and the account no longer offers “Use my own git repository”.

A logbook that was on the Subsurface cloud is not opened here: after an update from the alpha, the app starts from its first launch and leaves that logbook's files on the phone as they were. The Account page no longer offers signing in to the Subsurface cloud. A dive that cannot be read shows a page with « Try again ».

Logbook on a phone and on a tablet: dives are grouped by year, each year in a white card. Each row shows the date on a pale blue block, the site (or “Dive site not set” with a crossed-out pin), the dive number in bold and the time, the small profile, then the maximum depth in bold and the duration, in the units of the settings. A trip is its own card, with a pale blue header (suitcase, number of dives, depths) and an arrow to fold it. A screen reader reads each row as one item. On a tablet, trips are open in portrait and folded in landscape until you open or fold one yourself, and the dive shown keeps its pale blue background.

“Sign in or create an account”: the Google and Apple buttons now carry each provider’s official logo, on the phone, the tablet and the computer, with the colours of their brand rules. On a tablet and on a computer, the screen opens from “Sign in” on the first launch, in the two-pane layout.

Android: the screen edges are the same at every launch and in every navigation mode: sheets, messages, buttons and the bottom bar stay above the gesture bar or the navigation buttons, and the top no longer jumps.

Benthic server (release edition): your logbook downloads from the server and opens like any logbook, with « Your logbook is ready » after the download. It stays in Subsurface’s format, syncs like a git repository (automatic sync, offline, conflicts) and is named « Benthic server » in the menu, the account and the sync messages. « Create an empty logbook », « Import a Subsurface file » and « Send the logbook of this phone » create it on the server; an interrupted sending resumes where it stopped.

First launch on Android: the vertical spacing follows the mock-up (title, choices, buttons under the choices, « A question? » link) and the bottom link stays above the system navigation bar. Component styles again take precedence over Framework7's in the released build, which also fixes margins on other screens.

Equipment: “New piece” picks the type from tiles (computer, regulator, suit, undersuit, cylinder, BCD, lamp, weight belt, other) with a photo and a suggested service reminder; “Edit the kit” shows how many dives used the kit and lets you duplicate it; in “Edit the dive”, “Fill with” groups “A kit” and “Previous dive”.

Equipment service (Benthic+): “Service” in My profile and the card at the top of “Equipment” list what is overdue, coming up or up to date. A reminder can be set by time, by number of dives (those where the piece is in the equipment), or both: the first one reached counts. “Note a service” keeps the date, who did it, the cost and a photo of the invoice, and “Edit the dive” warns when a piece is overdue. A notification warns 7, 30 or 60 days before, then on the day.
Benthic+ offer: a « Service reminders » tile under the four others says that the regulator, cylinder and battery reminders arrive 30 days before they are due.

Logbook download and divelogs.de import: the time left shows on the right of the progress line when the operation takes more than 5 seconds, as « 20 s left », then in minutes. It replaces the earlier « About … » on the logbook upload.
Logbook: when the network comes back, the logbook leaves « Offline » and updates by itself, even with no change waiting, including when you return to the app.
Buttons: the touch effect shows on the pressed button, not at the top of the screen (seen in Clean up sites).
Offline maps: the dot on the account avatar goes away once a map update is done, including an update that finished while the app was closed.
Logbook: a progress bar shows at the top of the list while the app brings the logbook up to date at start; the list is already there.
Account sheet: the « Map update available » message is its own row, « Offline maps », and opens the offline maps in Settings directly.

My diver profile (Benthic+): the account sheet opens it, and « Equipment » holds your dive computers, regulators, suits, cylinders and kits, kept on this phone and readable offline. In « Edit dive », « Apply a kit » and « Same as the previous one » fill the equipment (with « Undo »), suits are picked from the inventory, a piece can be added for one dive only, and a dive computer can be renamed. A computer enters the inventory the first time you download from it.

First launch (public edition): « Sign in » is the first choice, in dark blue with the Benthic+ chip; « Start a logbook on this phone » and « Import a logbook » follow, then two text buttons, « Try with a sample logbook » and « Discover Benthic+ ». The choices have 24 dp corners, 24 sp titles on tablet and desktop, and the logo on the band has a thin light ring instead of a shadow. « New logbook » ends with « Create the logbook », the import with « Import the logbook ».

Benthic server (release edition): « On the Benthic server » is the first choice of « Open my logbook ». You sign in with your e-mail address and a 6-digit code, no password; the screens tell a wrong code, an expired code, too many attempts (10-minute wait) and a server that does not answer. The logbook is then downloaded.

First launch on Android tablets: « Use my own git repository » opens the form beside the blue panel, with « this tablet » in the texts; « How to create a repository » and « How to create an access token » replace the form in the same column, and « Back » brings it back with the fields filled. The logbook downloads, then opens with a message at the bottom left.

« Create a repository » and « Create an access token » help: the site's labels are in boxes and the values to type in a monospace font; the GitLab and Codeberg tabs give the site's labels in the app's language, and GitLab and Codeberg have their own token steps.
Sync with a git repository: a server that does not answer is no longer shown as a refused token; the app tries again on its own.

First launch and Compte on an Android phone: « Use my own git repository » is one form (address checked when you leave the field, token, the branches read from the repository), with the logbook download screen and then a message when it opens. The help « How to create a repository » gives the steps for GitHub, GitLab and Codeberg.

First launch (Android tablet): in landscape, the title and the dive profile on the left and the three choices on the right; in portrait, the title, the profile across the width, then the choices, centred. No scrolling, even on a small tablet.

Statistics: a total of time under water from 24 h is written in days and hours, without minutes ("80 d 16 h"), in the key figures, the "By …" and "My statistics" rows and the dives of a row; under 24 h it stays in hours and minutes.

Account (iPhone): signing in, creating an account, the confirmation code, bringing your logbook, the import and the git repository take the same layout as on Android: only “Cancel” or “Back” in the bar, a large title, rounded sections, a large capsule button and a dive profile.
Dive profile: the cursor is a plain line in the colour of the curve, without a white outline; the curve buttons (Temperature, ppO₂, Ceiling…) take the colour of their curve when selected.

Sites (tablet): the top of the list takes the band of the other sections, with the "N sites · M dives" summary, the faint profile and the wave; the map stays on the right, up to the top of the screen.
Statistics: the list of dives behind a row opens faster and uses far less memory on a large logbook; only the rows near the screen are drawn.
Dive: when you swipe to the next or previous dive, the site map and the details are already prepared; the screen arrives whole instead of filling in during the slide.

Account (Android): signing in, creating an account, the confirmation code, bringing your logbook and the git repository take the layout of first launch: a large title, the fields in a white card, a large button at the bottom and a dive profile. On a tablet, the title and the card sit side by side in landscape, one above the other in portrait.
Offline maps: they now work on iPhone and iPad too.
Statistics and dive: a value is no longer cut in the middle of a number or a word; when the key figures do not fit side by side, the last one moves whole to the next line.
Taps: a button, a menu or rail entry responds even if the finger slides a little while tapping; before, the tap was sometimes ignored.
Start-up: the app no longer stays on a white screen when it starts before its look has loaded.
Statistics: rows no longer show the maximum depth, and the name of a new statistic comes first.
Dives without a site: each dive shows a thumbnail of its profile and opens its full profile, with the buttons to give it a site.
Site sheet: each dive shows its number.
Statistics: the “By …” sections fold, and are closed at first. The charts and the rows of these sections no longer open anything, and the one-year view is gone.

Sites: the search opens from the magnifier with an animation. The field grows in the top bar, the count of matches sits under it, sites that do not match fade on the map, and the list shows only the results with the match highlighted. The back arrow, the back gesture or the back key closes it and brings the map back to where it was; the cross only clears the text. With reduced motion, the change is a short cross-fade.
Clean up sites: a pencil on each site of a duplicate group opens its editor, then returns to the same place; a group that no longer matches disappears.
Messages: one style for every snackbar, dark on light and light on dark, floating above the bottom of the screen (above the + button when there is one), with one action in blue.
Settings: resetting keeps your list of cylinders.
Clean up sites: "Not duplicates" removes the group from the list and stops suggesting it (on this device); "Undo" puts it back. Renaming or moving one of the two sites makes it suggestible again.
Settings: "Reset all settings" asks for confirmation first, then says "Settings reset". It no longer touches the planner settings.
Logo: the three waves now have shorter gradients, so the layers stay apart at small sizes.
Sites: a menu changes the order of the list (alphabetical or most recent first); a long press selects a site, to merge several sites.
Conflict on several dives: a full-screen dialog with a "Same choice for all" switch and one card per dive, where you touch the version to keep.
Sync conflict: "Later" closes the dialog and leaves you where you were; the Carnet sync status and the side menu sync card reopen it, and it comes back at the next sync attempt.
Offline maps: choosing an area opens on your current position.
Offline maps: an area with no logbook site takes the name of the place.
Offline maps: "Choose on the map" now shows a fixed frame; move and zoom the map under it and the area it covers is what you download. The detail is chosen for you, and the size shown is an estimate.
Offline maps: a search field on "Choose on the map" finds a site of your logbook as you type, or a place when you press search, and moves the map there.

Offline maps: choose an area on the map from Settings to download it (a frame of at most about 3,000 tiles); a space limit and a free-space floor protect the device, and updates are offered with a badge.
Privacy: the policy mentions searching for places on the map.
Offline maps: a search field on "Choose on the map" finds a site of your logbook as you type, or a place when you press search, and puts the rectangle around it.
Offline maps: frame an area on the map from Settings to download it; a space limit and a free-space floor protect the device, and updates are offered with a badge.
Logbook: while scrolling, the current month shows at the top under the bar.
Settings: the water type written on downloaded dives that have none can be chosen (Not specified by default).
Sites: without a network, the map reads the downloaded regions, else a simplified world map; an "Offline" pill says so and a message offers to download the area.
Desaturation: the text under the chart is shorter.
Settings: the app language can be Français (Canada), which says "nuage" and "courriel"; a phone set to French (Canada) picks it by itself.
Dive detail: the cylinder pressure bars run from 0 to the working pressure, with what is left and what was used.
Planner: a plan made from a rebreather dive starts on the diluent, never the oxygen.
Planner: a bar shows the consumed part and the reserve of each gas, another the CNS exposure.
Statistics: charts that do not measure depth (dives per year, durations) are blue.
Editing a rebreather dive: no gas switch depth for the diluent and oxygen, and choosing the use fills in the starting mix (21 % or 100 %).
Sites: the header has the same wave and profile as the other sections, and the map shows under the curve.
Logbook: the sync state (offline with changes waiting, failure, conflict) shows in a pill in the header; a dive waiting to be sent keeps its number and date.
Sync: when it fails while the network works, the Logbook says why (password refused, cloud not answering, git repository refused) and offers what to do.
Planner: the starting dive shows its number and duration, in the planner and in the list to choose it.
Planner settings: no introduction line, the groups follow the title directly.
Planner: “New dive” without the line “Defaults of the Subsurface planner”.
Settings: new group “Default conditions” (water type and altitude), used by the planner and the gas calculator.
Planner redone: planned dives saved in the logbook, several levels and gases, volumes per gas, a decompression model for each plan, sharing a plan.
Edit dive: every cylinder shows all its fields, no collapsed lines.
Share: a PDF icon for the sheet. Export: the first format is named “Logbook file (.ssrf)”.
About: each open source library opens its website in the browser.
Planner: the reserve has a SAC factor under stress (1.0 by default) and a number of divers on the gas (1 by default, 2 to ascend as two); the result says so.

Settings: default cylinders for open circuit and rebreather (diluent, oxygen, bailout), added when a dive becomes a rebreather dive. Cylinder types: number of dives and a new form. Profile: ceilings reordered, depth grid removed.
Side menu and headers redone: band, account at the top of the menu, centred sync, a summary for each section, logbook search bar. Settings and About use the ☰ menu.
Logbook: rows aligned with the design (no dividers), the dives of an expanded trip in a white surface. Account: same header as the sections.
Logbook: a trip of one dive is shown as a dive, without an arrow.
Logbook: while dragging a dive, a horizontal bar shows where it would be dropped.
Logbook: the dive number is back before the date; an open trip is indented, and its dives can be checked in selection mode.
Logbook: a trip can be selected; “Delete this trip” removes the trip and keeps its dives.
Privacy policy: links and the contact address can be tapped.
Secure connections: the OpenSSL library is replaced by Mbed TLS, compatible with the app’s licence.

Git repository: the logbook can live in your own git repository (GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg or your server) instead of the Subsurface cloud. On the first page, “Use my own git repository”; the access token stays encrypted on the device.
Tablet: the logbook opens the first dive when none is shown.
Sharing: the app no longer stays stuck under a grey veil after sharing a dive or a plan.
Dive profile: the card follows the mock-up (full-width chart, scale down to the maximum depth).
Planner: a saved plan keeps its rates, reserve and other settings, and gives the same result when reopened.
Settings: the units chosen on the device no longer go back to the logbook’s at restart.
Dive detail: the screen follows the mock-up (top bar, trip as a link, sizes and margins, people and tags as chips, a dot on the temperature curve at the cursor).
Dive detail: map of the site behind the header, prepared ahead on Wi-Fi, when the site has GPS coordinates.
Dive detail: a dive on its own no longer shows a trip.
Dive detail: the rating stars stand alone.
Dive detail: “Remove from trip” in the ⋮ menu.
About: the map credit also names OpenFreeMap and OpenMapTiles.
Edit a dive: sections always open, the trip chosen from a list, with a button to remove it.
Edit a dive: choose the main computer when the dive has several.
Settings: Logbook dive computers, to rename, remove or merge duplicates, found by serial number, then by comparing the profiles.
Logbook: “Logbook dive computers” in the ⋮ menu.

New logo, a deep-blue disc with a white wave and a soft relief (light rim, shadow under the wave): app icon, launch screen, menu and About. The favicon is simplified so that it stays readable at 16 px.
Sync conflict: new dialog, readable differences, “Later”, and “Undo” before anything is sent.
Filter (Android): new page, cylinder and gas criteria grouped, a saved filter fills the page, and deleting one offers “Undo”.
Filter: the explanatory sentences under the criteria are gone.
What’s new: the version date next to its number, and the complete list.
Statistics: each row opens the list of its dives.
Logbook: the month shown in the band is more discreet.
Navigation buttons react to a touch at once.
Durations of an hour or more follow the language: “1:11” in English, “1 h 11” in French.
Settings: the “Always in hours and minutes” duration option is gone.
Desaturation: the last logbook dive, and “You can fly” once the wait is over.
Dive rows: the duration above, the depth below.
Settings: the chosen unit system stays after a restart.
First launch (Android): a simpler page, with three buttons and their consequence on one line.
Access token help: one tab per host (GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg).
First launch: full screen on tablets, every choice in view.
Tablet: after signing out, the account’s last dive no longer stays beside the empty logbook.
Tablet: Settings and About open full width, no longer beside the logbook list.
Tablet: section headers get their wavy edge back.
Best mix: « Prepare this mix » opens the Gas blender with that mix as the wanted mix (on a tablet, the button names the mix).

Gas blender: « Desired final pressure » (was « Final pressure ») starts at the working pressure of the chosen cylinder, shown as « Working pressure: 3,365 psi ». A typed value stays when the cylinder changes; above the working pressure a warning shows and the calculation goes on.

Gas blender: the cylinder is chosen before the final pressure; « In the cylinder » puts Pressure and Mix (nitrox) or Oxygen and Helium (trimix); the note on pressures is no longer red; « Analyse the mix before diving. » is in an amber banner.

Public edition: an account with no logbook offers to create an empty logbook, import a Subsurface file (.ssrf or .xml) or send the logbook of the device. The logbook is written in Benthic' format on the server, in small uploads; it also stays on the device.

Public edition: the upload shows « n dives of m » and the time left. If the connection drops, « Upload interrupted » says so and « Resume the upload » restarts after the last dive sent; the upload is also offered again at the next start.

Public edition: « Sign in or create an account », the Benthic+ offer (US $14.99 a year), « Your logbook is ready » and « Welcome to Benthic+! ». Signing in with Google or Apple and subscribing are not available yet; an account without a subscription keeps nothing on the device.
Public edition: the server screens no longer show « Benthic server » above the title, the « The server is not responding » icon is centred and « Back to the start » replaces « Choose another place ».

In the desktop app, you can resize a Logbook column by dragging the edge of its header (or ← → on the edge, a double click to fit it), and each logbook keeps its own column order, visible columns and widths on this computer.

In the desktop app, « Only on Wi-Fi or cable » now works: the automatic sync waits while the computer is on a metered connection (a phone's hotspot, mobile broadband) and runs when it is back on Wi-Fi or cable; « Sync now » still works.

Lighter start-up and faster dive selection: the app loads half as much code and style at start, each screen and each language when it is first needed, and selecting a dive in the desktop logbook asks the core for that dive only instead of eighteen answers.

In the desktop app, a long dive's profile is drawn with a few points per pixel instead of every sample, and the window no longer keeps the other layout in memory after you resize it across the narrow and wide layouts.
In the desktop app, a large logbook is fast: the Logbook table draws only the rows in view, so selecting a dive, searching, sorting and coming back to the Logbook stay quick with thousands of dives.

Desktop dive detail: five tabs. Information has the site card, buddies, guide, a segmented water type and five-star visibility; Equipment has the computers, the suit and several weights as chips with their total; Gas has one card per cylinder with its fields and a Consumption card; Notes has the rating, notes and tags; Map keeps its height. Grey fields save when you press Enter or leave them.

In the desktop app, resizing the window across 1200 dp switches between the wide and the narrow layout without leaving the screen: the dive selected in the Logbook, the saved statistic in Statistics, the category in Settings and the tool in Tools stay as they were.
In the desktop app, a window opened for another logbook stays inside the screen, so the account button at the foot of the left bar is never cut off.

Phone, « Your logbook is ready » (Benthic+): the logo turns twice and becomes a check mark, with a ring that spreads out, while the bubbles of the header rise and leave; it plays once, the first time the screen shows. With reduced motion, the check mark is shown at once and the bubbles stay still. The header also has the dive profile above its wave.

My diver profile (Benthic+): “Information” keeps your date of birth, your emergency contact (the number formats itself for the country) and your blood group, encrypted on this phone. You can enter or clear your blood group by editing “Information”. “Certifications” keeps your cards with their front and back photos, without a network; the phone’s document scanner frames and straightens each card, then the app reads the agency, the level, the number and the date from it, for you to check. The service reminder suggested for a regulator is now yearly.

Equipment: the BCD has its own icon (collar, centre opening, two straps) and the surface marker buoy its own, with a flat top. In « New piece » (and when editing), a thumbnail left of the « Model » field shows your photo of the piece, otherwise the icon of its type, large.

Files from another app: Benthic is in “Open with” and “Share to” for a logbook (.ssrf, .xml), a UDDF, FIT or DLD file and the other formats it imports. The file is read, then a choice is asked: “Add to this logbook” adds the dives to the open logbook, with Undo (“New logbook”, which keeps the open logbook and creates another, is not offered: this device keeps one logbook at a time); with no logbook yet it opens “Import a logbook”. The sites file of a two-file export is accepted: sites already there are not duplicated. The sites go to the logbook named in the question, never to another one.

First launch: the slide between steps now plays (it was dropped from the build). The waiting-changes box of the sign-out dialog shows its count in bold, and an iPhone field in error no longer keeps a red frame inside its row.

Replace this logbook: this device keeps one logbook at a time. A logbook file (Subsurface .ssrf, or an archive holding one) opened with Benthic or chosen in “+” › Import a file now offers “Replace this logbook”: a screen says the logbook leaves this device and offers “Export this logbook first”; “Replace” asks a second time when it was not exported or when changes are not synchronised, then you name the new logbook. The current logbook is put back if the file cannot be read. The Benthic server logbook and a logbook synchronised with an account are never replaced, with a line that says why. When an archive holds several logbooks, only the main one is imported and the dialog says so.

Large logbooks: a logbook of a thousand dives with profiles (about 100 MB) can now be shared to Benthic from another app, picked with “Import a file”, used to replace the logbook, exported first, copied from the previous version or included in “Download my data” without the app running out of memory. The file now goes straight between the phone’s storage and the core in small pieces instead of passing through the screen as one text.

Import: a logbook or a dive sites file shows one progress line, from the moment it is received or chosen until the import is finished: “Copying the file”, “Checking the file”, “Importing the dives”, “Saving”, with the size copied, the percentage and the time left. “Cancel” stops the copy and the check and deletes the partial copy. A message tells how many dives or sites were added.
Dive page: after swiping to the neighbouring dive, Back no longer leaves the page half-way through its transition with the logbook shifted aside; Back pressed while a swipe settles is ignored.

Settings, Cylinder types: a type of “Your types” has a “Delete this type” button, with the number of dives that use it. Deleting it removes its cylinders, with their pressures and gas mix, from the dives that use it; the confirmation says how many dives lose the cylinder. Where the cylinder is the dive’s only one, or a gas switch or the pressure graph depends on it, it stays in the dive with the type “Unknown type”. A type used in no dive is deleted at once. Standard types still only have “Remove this type”, which changes no dive.

Units: gas consumption per minute follows the Volume unit. In cubic feet it is in cu ft/min (SAC, RMV and the metabolic O₂ consumption of the pSCR in Settings), in litres in L/min, converted from the same stored value. Under “Volume”, a line says so.

Desktop: « Other gear » on the Equipment tab shows the pieces of your inventory used by the dive, with the same icon as on the phone (the « Saucisse » has its own), « Add gear » adds them and the cross removes them from this dive. Every desktop logbook view (map, tabs, menus, windows) shares the same list: weekday, one year line that stays at the top, trip cards.

Cylinders on desktop: Settings › Equipment shows « Cylinders added to new dives » (open circuit, diluent, oxygen, bailout with « Edit ») and « Cylinder types » (your types with their dive counts, a few standard types then « And N other standard types… », « Add a type », and the two switches). A type opens in the « Edit type » dialog, with « Delete this type » at the left of the footer and the same confirmation as on the phone. On the phone, the explanation and the line under « Delete this type » sit on the 16 dp margin, and « Remove this type » stays a neutral button.

iPhone: the logbook has no blue band any more, with a large title, a grey search field, « + » and the account initial in the bar. The « Account » sheet follows the mock-ups (« Logbook on this iPhone », « Subscribe », « Manage account », the Benthic+ dot, « My diver profile » with its overdue maintenance). The profile and cylinder type screens show the previous page's title on the Back button, with « + » in the bar. « Delete this type » is a red row, and the deletion is confirmed in an action sheet. « Open in Maps » opens the site in Apple Maps. « Continue with Apple » comes first, and the offer adds « Restore purchases » and the automatic renewal terms (the purchase and the sign-in with Apple are not active yet).

First launch: the Android Back key and gesture (and, on iPhone, a swipe from the left edge) go to the previous step, like “Back”; on the first step Back sends the app to the background. A running import, download or upload is cancelled by Back, the offer’s Back is “Continue without a subscription”, and nothing created or bought is undone.

Other equipment: adding or removing a piece on a dive is for Benthic+ subscribers. Without an account the list shows with the Benthic+ chip, on the phone, the tablet and the desktop, and cannot be changed.
Account sheet (free version): Back from the Benthic+ offer or from “Sign in or create an account”, opened from the sheet, shows the sheet again as it was.

Backup and restore (Benthic+): a subscriber’s account sheet lists “My diver profile”, then “Backup and restore”, with no Benthic+ chip next to the rows. Every sync is a version of the logbook, with its number of dives and what changed since. “Restore this version” adds a new version with the old content: the current logbook stays in the list and can be restored in turn, and nothing of the history is rewritten. “Browse this version” opens it read-only. “One dive” shows the versions of a dive (also from “Versions of this dive” in its menu) and “Deleted dives” brings a deleted dive back, with no time limit. Deleted photos and videos are kept for 90 days, then erased, and “Delete the account” also erases the whole history of the logbook, deleted dives included. On a phone these are pages, on a tablet two panes, on a computer a 1,000 px dialog.

Error reports: after an error or a crash, the version, system, device, open page, error message and last lines of the log appear in a sheet with “Send” and “Don’t send”. Nothing is sent without that tap; without a connection the report is kept and offered again later. A report contains no dive, site, name or account; it is kept 180 days.
Export of the whole logbook: the file is named after the logbook and the date, for example “carnet-de-roger-2026-11-19.ssrf”.

Benthic+ offer: the header now reads “The Benthic+ plan” with “Your logbook, safe on all your devices.”, the cards have more room (on a tablet the icon sits to the left of the text), and the price is plain text, not a blue card, with “Cancel any time”. The new “See everything included” link opens the “Everything included” screen: the subscription’s features by group, what stays free, and the price with “Subscribe” that stays at the bottom while you scroll. On a tablet, “Already subscribed? Sign in” moves to the top right, on the row of “Back”.

About: “Open-source dive logbook, built on the solid, proven foundations of Subsurface.”, a block “Free, and so is your logbook” (the base plan stays free, the code is on GitHub, the logbook can be exported at any time) with “See on GitHub” (the GitHub mark) and “Export my logbook” (a download icon), one under the other on a phone and side by side on a tablet; on the desktop, one paragraph and the two buttons. “Everything included” says under its title what it lists.

Tablet in landscape and desktop: “My diver profile” shows in panes: the profile on the left, the list (equipment or maintenance) in the middle, the sheet on the right. The forms (new piece, new kit, new certification, note a service) open in a centred dialog; the piece types form a 3 × 3 grid. On the desktop, the photo of a certification is chosen, dropped or pasted (Ctrl+V); the card is cropped and straightened, with “Remove glare” and “Adjust the corners”. On a Mac, “My diver profile…” (⇧⌘P) opens the profile in its own window. “Your logbook is ready” appears in the blue panel. On the desktop, the logbook’s + no longer stays over a page opened on the right.

Desktop: the account sheet of an Benthic+ subscriber is redone: the logo at the top, the account (avatar with the +, “Manage the account” aligned with the text, the sync line with “Sync”), then “My diver profile” and “Backup and restore”, then Settings and About, each with its icon in a blue tile.

Desktop: “Share” opens as a dialog in the middle of the window; a click on a trip in the logbook shows the trip page on the right (the chevron folds it); importing a file says where the dives come from (“1 dive imported from “…””) with Undo; “Saved plans” opens a “Planned dives” side panel with “New plan”; in Settings › Rebreather, the O₂ consumption says it follows the Volume unit.

Tablet: “Export” and the list of dives at one map point open as a dialog in the middle of the screen, and so do conflicts on several dives; when downloading, a Bluetooth that is not allowed or is off shows as a card under the remembered computers.
iPad: the same dialogs and the same Bluetooth card as on the Android tablet, with iOS sheet corners.
iPhone: About has 50 pt buttons with iOS rounded corners; tablet in portrait: in Offline maps, “Add a region” moves under the list.
Sample logbook: 40 dives from 2023 to 2026 at 8 sites, with a trip of 6 dives and a rebreather dive, closer to a real logbook.

Sample logbook on a phone: the “Sample logbook. These dives are not yours.” banner is a rounded card just above the bottom bar, with “Start”; the list, the + and the messages stop above it. “Start my logbook?” names the device (this phone, this tablet, this computer).

Empty logbook: the header reads “On this phone · no dives” (“My logbook · on this tablet” on a tablet) and “Change location” is gone from the menu. Desktop with a git repository: the account sheet shows the repository with “Change repository”, the sync row, “Backup and restore” (following the repository’s history) and the “Upgrade to Benthic+” card, without “My diver profile”.
Desktop: a trip of a single dive is no longer a trip row in the logbook, as on the phone.
Dive computers show their photo (dive detail, download choice, Equipment); it is downloaded once, then kept on the device. With no photo, or offline, the icon stays.
“This ballast was” is now a rail: a pill slides from one choice to the next; touching the chosen choice clears it.
Equipment: “Edit the dive computer” (brand and model with suggestions, or free text; “Change image” keeps your photo in your account, not shared).

iPhone: the logbook has no profile thumbnail (day and month, “No. · time”, depth over duration, year titles with their dive count); Settings with a large title and small-capitals groups; a site's page in grouped cards, with “Open in Maps” explained; About and Open-source libraries with a named back button.
Benthic+ offer: the header follows its design (logo and name, chip, a 24-point title, still bubbles) and “See everything included” is centred.

Dive computer photos show wherever the model appears: the equipment, kits and maintenance lists, the part sheet, the dive detail, Réglages › Dive computers of the logbook and the dive edit. Your own photo wins over the model’s.

After a download from a dive computer that is not in your equipment (Benthic+), a card offers to add it: “Later” or “Add”. A logbook computer and an equipment piece are the same when brand, model and serial number match.

Deleting a dive computer asks “Delete the … ?”; “New piece” of type Dive computer has brand and model suggestions, the model’s photo and no maintenance reminder; “Edit the dive computer” follows each device; Réglages › Edit the dive computer is restyled (image, duplicate and remove cards).

After a download from a dive computer, “Complete the dive” opens for each new dive without a site (Android and iPhone): the three nearest sites by distance from the phone, or the three most recently dived without a position, with the nearest one preselected within 500 m, “Create a site at my current position”, “Search for another site”, buddies and the rating. “Later” leaves the dive as it is.

Réglages › Notifications (Benthic+): maintenance reminders, a default lead time of 2 weeks, 30 or 60 days, “Remind me when late” once a week until the maintenance is recorded, and “Flight allowed”. Notifications arrive at 9:00 (except the flight one) with the buttons “View”, “Record the service” and “Remind me in 1 week”. A reminder’s lead time is now 14, 30 or 60 days; “Pre-trip check” is gone, and a dive computer has no reminder any more.

Equipment (Benthic+): “Retire from equipment” takes an optional reason (sold, lost, worn out). A retired piece leaves the lists, the kits and the reminders but keeps its service history and its dives; it is found in “Retired pieces”, where it can be put back in service, have its history exported as a PDF, or be deleted for good. “Export the history” is also in a piece’s menu.

A cylinder has two deadlines, each with its own card, bar, “Record …” button and reminder: the visual inspection (every year) and the hydrostatic test (every 5 years, with the date stamped on the cylinder, like 03/22). The maintenance card also shows the hours under water next to the dives (“82 dives out of 100 · 61 h”). In “Add equipment”, an overdue piece stays selectable but says in red what is late, when its reminder warns in a dive.
Downloading from a dive computer no longer freezes the screen when the error report sheet opens.
On Windows, “Edit dive” and the quick entry now save every site: some sites (more than half of them) could not be found when saving.

Account: choosing “Subscriber” in the development menu (or any Benthic+ subscription) now makes the account sheet the subscriber’s one at once, whatever the place of the logbook. “My diver profile” opens the profile, and “Backup and restore” says that the logbook is only on this device, with “Send the logbook to the server”.

Download: a lamp or a scale whose name starts with “S1” (“S19 A69C LE”) is no longer offered as an Oceans S1. Each device in the nearby list has a menu with “This is not a dive computer”, which hides it for good (Undo in the message); Settings › Download lists the hidden devices with “Show again”.
Android: the Back key works while a message such as “Dive saved / Undo” is on screen; it was ignored until the message disappeared.

Equipment: « New piece » offers 16 types (mask, fins, scooter, camera, surface marker buoy, surface float and knife are added) and shows only the fields of the chosen type; only the type is required. A cylinder keeps its type (volume and working pressure come from Settings › Equipment), material, valve, serial number, « O₂ clean », last visual inspection and last hydrostatic test; a suit, its type, thickness, size and material. The BCD is now called « Vest » (« Veste » in French) everywhere. Reminders suggested: regulator every 2 years or 100 dives, cylinder (inspection every year, hydrostatic test every 5 years), vest every year, drysuit seals every year.

Certifications and documents: « Certifications » becomes « Certifications and documents »: certifications, diving insurance (card scanned and read on the device, or a PDF), a medical certificate of several pages and other documents, each with a reproduction of the card and an expiry badge. A document opens full screen at maximum brightness and is shared as images or as a PDF. A certification can be marked « Instructor certification ».

Notifications: Settings › Notifications has a « Certifications and documents » section with « Document expiry ». The notification comes at the lead time chosen in each document (2 weeks, 30 days or 60 days) and on the day it expires.
Benthic+ offer: the price is a little smaller, and the « Service reminders » tile mentions the regulator, the cylinder and the vest.
Edit dive: the suggestion lists of Guide, Buddies and Tags (and of the suit) now open above the following cards, inside the screen, and above the field when there is no room below.
Logbook: on Android, the floating toolbar of a selection sits above the bottom navigation bar (and above the sample logbook banner) instead of under it.

Dive validation (Benthic+): “Get the dive signed” in the dive menu, and “Get the dives signed” in the selection menu (one validation for several dives). The buddy or instructor signs with a finger on the screen, or scans a QR code with Benthic+ (the code expires after 10 minutes; without a network, the dive shows “Validation pending” until the confirmation arrives). The dive detail has a “Validations” section (name, role, method, date, signature) and says “Changed after the validation” when the dive changed; a validated dive carries a small tick in the logbook. Validations appear on the PDF sheet and in the logbook’s PDF export, and can be removed one by one.

Navigation: a swipe from the edge of the screen (Android’s Back gesture) no longer leaves the page half moved, with Back and links doing nothing; the Back that follows goes back one screen. Going back twice from a screen opened deep in the Logbook (Settings › Cylinder types › new type; a dive › its planner › the plans › a new plan) no longer leaves an empty screen where Back does nothing. A screen left in a wrong state is put back in place and an error report is offered. The Escape key closes the open sheet, dialog or menu. “Question / report a problem” adds the last screens visited to the message.

My diver profile: an optional “Full name” field, first in “You” of Information and its edit screen. It shows at the top of “My diver profile” (the e-mail without it) and, with an Benthic+ account, on the first line of the account sheet, with the e-mail under it in smaller grey text. When you confirm another diver’s dive, “Your name” comes from the profile (a correction applies to that confirmation only), the sentence under it gives your role and your instructor certification number, and “I confirm” stays off while the name is empty; if the profile has no name, the name you type is saved there. The name is added at the top of the PDF sheets of a dive and of the logbook (switch “My name in the header” when exporting a PDF; “Anonymize” removes it too).

“New piece”: on a phone, “Piece type” is a field that opens a menu of the 16 types (icon, name, a check on the chosen type; the system list on iPhone); the grid of tiles stays on tablets and desktop. Under the field, the model’s photo, large, with “Change image” (the type’s drawing when the model has no photo; “Add a photo” and the small thumbnail beside “Model” are gone). Five icons redrawn everywhere in the equipment: weight belt, scooter, knife, fins and light.

Dates: every date follows the format chosen in Settings › Language and date (2026-11-06 by default): logbook, dive detail, equipment and maintenance, certificates and documents, validation, account, backup, offline maps, PDF. Date fields show that format as their hint (“yyyy-mm-dd”), typing in the calendar follows it, and a date known to the month only (hydrostatic test) is written in the same order (2022-03).

Emergency sheet (Benthic+): a red “Emergency sheet” entry under the identity card of “My diver profile” opens a full-screen sheet that works without a network: the profile’s full name, date of birth and age, the blood type in a tile, the emergency contact with “Call Marc” (opens the phone’s dialer), the diving insurance with its “Emergency line” and the medical certificate, which open the document. The pencil opens “Sheet content”: one switch for each item (the highest certificate starts off), the name is always shown. Sharing sends the sheet as an image or a PDF, with the reminder that it contains the blood type. In “Information”, when editing, the emergency contact has two fields, “Name” and “Relationship” (a menu that also takes free text).

Dive detail: on Android the floating toolbar holds Edit, “Plan from this dive”, Share and a ⋮ menu (“Get the dive signed” with Benthic+, “Renumber the dive”, “Remove from trip” in a trip, “Delete the dive”). The ⋮ button’s name lists what its menu holds.
Site map: in a site’s card, on the edit screen and on the desktop, the map keeps a 2.1 to 1 width to height ratio at every width; the height follows the width.

Emergency sheet: the certificate shown is your most recent card (latest issue date), whatever its level or type; with the same date, the one added last. The switch in “Sheet content” is named “Most recent certificate”.

Cards and documents: a scan now reads more from the card, on the device only. A certification card gives the agency (also RAID, PSS, ANMP), the level, the number, the date and the instructor, with both sides read together; an insurance card gives the insurer, plan, number, emergency phone and dates; a medical certificate gives the doctor, the date and the expiry; another document gives its title and expiry. Each value is marked “to check”, a field you typed is never replaced, and nothing is shown when the text is unclear. The scanned picture now always appears in its slot (it was lost on Android when the scan was large).
New name: the app is now called Benthic, and the paid offer Benthic+. The name under the icon is “Benthic Log”. Old opendives.app links still open the app.

Certifications: the agency menu now lists many more agencies (recreational, technical, freediving and national federations), and the level suggestions cover the whole ladder of the main agencies, from entry level to instructor. A photo or scan slot now shows a progress indicator while the picture is read, and the picture appears at once.

Information (Benthic+): the page is edited in place. The pencil turns the sections into fields, “Save” is in the top bar and Back leaves without saving. An empty value no longer shows any text. On a tablet and the desktop, the sections have a horizontal margin.
Tablet and desktop: the Account button, at the bottom of the sidebar, is larger.
Dive profile: no curve is on by default any more, the water temperature included; turn on the ones you want, the choice is kept.
Tablet and desktop: at start, the right pane shows the shape of the dive while the logbook is read, instead of “Choose a dive to see it here”.

github.name: GitHub
github.intro: Benthic connects to your repository with a personal access token, never with your password. Create a token limited to this one repository, allowed to read and write its contents and nothing else. GitHub exists only in English: the labels below are those of its interface.
github.note: A fine-grained token can be limited to a single repository.
github.s1: Sign in to GitHub, then open [kbd]Settings[/kbd] (menu of your profile picture).
github.s2: At the bottom of the left column, open [kbd]Developer settings[/kbd].
github.s3: Open [kbd]Personal access tokens[/kbd], then [kbd]Fine-grained tokens[/kbd], then tap [kbd]Generate new token[/kbd].
github.s3Desktop: Open [kbd]Personal access tokens[/kbd], then [kbd]Fine-grained tokens[/kbd], then click [kbd]Generate new token[/kbd].
github.s4: [kbd]Token name[/kbd]: a name you will recognise, for example [code]Benthic[/code].
github.s5: [kbd]Expiration[/kbd]: choose [kbd]No expiration[/kbd], otherwise Benthic can no longer sync on the chosen date. If the repository belongs to an organisation, it may impose an end date.
github.s6: [kbd]Resource owner[/kbd]: your account, or the organisation that owns the repository.
github.s7: [kbd]Repository access[/kbd]: choose [kbd]Only select repositories[/kbd], then the repository of your logbook.
github.s8: [kbd]Permissions[/kbd]: under [kbd]Repository permissions[/kbd], set [kbd]Contents[/kbd] to [kbd]Read and write[/kbd]. Add no other permission.
github.s9: Tap [kbd]Generate token[/kbd], then copy the token.
github.s9Desktop: Click [kbd]Generate token[/kbd], then copy the token.

gitlab.name: GitLab
gitlab.intro: Benthic connects to your repository with a personal access token, never with your password. Create a token that can only read and write your repositories. The labels below are those of the site’s English interface.
gitlab.note: On GitLab, a personal token gives access to all your repositories and must have an expiry date.
gitlab.s1: Sign in to GitLab, tap your avatar, then [kbd]Edit profile[/kbd].
gitlab.s1Desktop: Sign in to GitLab, click your avatar, then [kbd]Edit profile[/kbd].
gitlab.s2: In the left sidebar, open [kbd]Access[/kbd], then [kbd]Personal access tokens[/kbd].

gitlab.s4: [kbd]Token name[/kbd]: a name you will recognise, for example [code]Benthic[/code].
gitlab.s5: [kbd]Expiration date[/kbd]: choose the latest date allowed. GitLab requires a date; on that date, create a new token and paste it into Benthic.
gitlab.s6: [kbd]Select scopes[/kbd]: tick only [kbd]write_repository[/kbd], which allows reading and writing in your repositories.
gitlab.s7: Tap [kbd]Generate token[/kbd], then copy the token.
gitlab.s7Desktop: Click [kbd]Generate token[/kbd], then copy the token.
